The shoelace determinant simplifies to signed area \(=4\lambda^2+2\lambda-2\). Setting \(|4\lambda^2+2\lambda-2|=70\): the \(+70\) branch gives \(2\lambda^2+\lambda-36=0 \Rightarrow \lambda=4\) or \(-\tfrac92\); the \(-70\) branch has discriminant \(1-272<0\), no real root. Only \(\lambda=4\) is integral. Check \(\lambda=4\): vertices \((4,-6),(-3,8),(-8,-2)\) give area \(\tfrac12|40-12+112|=70\). So 1 value.

working: Partial fractions: \(\frac{x-1}{(x-3)(x-2)}=\frac{2}{x-3}-\frac{1}{x-2}\) (at \(x=3\), \(A=2\); at \(x=2\), \(B=-1\)). Integrating gives \(2\log(x-3)-\log(x-2)+c=\log(x-3)^{2}-\log(x-2)+c\). Differentiation of (B) returns the integrand exactly.

\(\frac{1}{x^{2}+b^{2}}-\frac{1}{x^{2}+a^{2}}=\frac{a^{2}-b^{2}}{(x^{2}+a^{2})(x^{2}+b^{2})}\), so the integrand is \(\frac{1}{a^{2}-b^{2}}\left[\frac{1}{x^{2}+b^{2}}-\frac{1}{x^{2}+a^{2}}\right]\), integrating to \(\frac{1}{a^{2}-b^{2}}\left[\frac1b\tan^{-1}\frac{x}{b}-\frac1a\tan^{-1}\frac{x}{a}\right]+c\). Symbolic differentiation of (A) minus the integrand simplifies to 0; (B) has the sign of the prefactor reversed.
